dedupe_keys.name: fcc antenna structure registration asr data

description: Antenna Structure Registration is the FCC's register of antenna structures in the United States that are taller than 200 feet above ground or near airports and that the Federal Aviation Administration says need painting or lighting. Owners register each tower with its location, height above ground and above mean sea level, structure type, owner, FAA study number, painting and lighting requirements and construction and dismantlement dates, and the FCC publishes the registrations with the Universal Licensing System data. Coverage: the United States and territories, tens of thousands of tall structures such as broadcast and cellular towers, with history of registrations. Format and access: the weekly complete registration file (r_tower.zip, about 38 MB) and daily files as pipe-delimited text on data.fcc.gov, plus online search; free as US government data. Caveats: only tall or airport-adjacent structures are included, so most cell sites are absent; the antennas and tenants on a structure are not listed. Simulation uses: an asset inventory of tall communication towers for exposure to wind, ice, earthquake and wildfire and for broadcast and backhaul resilience studies. Related records: ULS licence data give the transmitters, and the monopole tower fragility dataset gives damage functions.
